scene: communication-limited observation (2 evaders, 2 gates, 3 pursuers, real 2-D kinematics)
finding: Sharp phase transition at R ~ 3.2-3.5 (the pursuer->own-evader distance). Below it, NO local policy succeeds (can't see target); above it, ALL succeed including greedy. There is NO regime where 'division of labour' separates local_greedy from local_ideal: when an evader is visible, every pursuer chases the nearest and the geometry splits them naturally; when not visible, no division signal helps.

vs_three_walls.W1_follow_saturates: Avoided only trivially: at small R local fails because it CANNOT see (no follow possible), but at large R follow saturates (all 1.0) - same wall as before, just pushed to R.
vs_three_walls.W2_leakage: No clean regime: either position leaks enough that greedy is optimal, or comm hides so much that even ideal division fails.
vs_three_walls.W3_feasible_vs_decisive: Feasibility fine (oracle 1.0 everywhere), but there is NO decisive window where division matters.

conclusion: With this geometry (each pursuer ~ one evader's lane), communication limit is a binary switch, not a tunable 'division-of-labour matters' regime. Greedy nearest-chase already achieves the optimal division whenever sensing suffices. To make division NON-trivial, evaders must be able to swap lanes / be ambiguous which pursuer should cover which (assignment genuinely multi-modal), not merely invisible sometimes. This probe does NOT yet demonstrate that scene 3 escapes the earlier walls.
